significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish the form-(iii) predictive coupling that models with higher "Relational-Fidelity Score" systematically generalize better to "held-out entities and relations," alongside the representational phenomenon that their embedding geometry recovers known lattices, clusters, or tree metrics. This fixes expected rankings of models and layers on untested entity-generalization tasks, a weightier conclusion than merely decoding scientific concepts; however, it establishes a correlational representational phenomenon rather than a causal mechanism, and probing literature such as Belinkov (2022) cautions that decodability alone does not show that a representation drives behavior. Verified false, it would rule out the proposed broad read-only diagnostic, although heterogeneous null results would not rule out ontology representations individually; true and false are distinguishable through the stated directional fidelity–generalization relationship, while "genuine structural understanding" remains less determinate. Topic substitution leaves only the generic question of whether models represent scientific structure, which would not merit this score; the specific cross-ontology predictive coupling is the above-median increment.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "Relational-Fidelity Score combining axis-recovery R^2, cluster purity, and metric-correlation," proposed as a "read-only diagnostic" that predicts held-out generalization; this is ex ante when used to compare or screen models before attempting rare or synthetic entities, rather than solely explaining failures afterward. After per-model extraction, the conclusion still predicts a transferable directional relation—higher fidelity should imply better generalization—rather than merely supplying a procedure for rediscovering an unconstrained direction, although the claim specifies no transferable threshold or effect size. Its asserted scope spans chemistry, biology, and materials ontologies and multiple model classes, giving potential uptake to model auditors and selectors as well as representation researchers; this is materially broader than scientific-model work such as ESM-2 (Lin et al., 2023), where learned representations are principally validated through domain tasks rather than offered as a general ontology-fidelity gate. Under topic substitution, neither this score nor the audit handle survives: the generic topic supplies no cross-domain metric, lead time, or fidelity-to-generalization prediction.
